spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers; u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m jointly smooth, q unit. Assume |u|=1, u_tt−Δ_xu=a u pointwise and u=q outside a compact set uniformly on every compact time interval. Set e=|u_t|²+Σ|∂_xj u|², E=∫R^n e dx. Prove e(·,r) integrable, E differentiable, E'(r)=0 for r>0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

propositions.statement: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

locals.declaration: Choose the compact set from H003.

argument.text: Fix r>0, choose compact interval J with r interior and C_J by H003. Smoothness and constancy imply derivatives vanish outside C_J and on its boundary, so e is continuous compactly supported. M001 proves integrability. Choose box B containing C_J. e_t is continuous on compact B×J; M004 gives uniform continuity. M002 represents the time difference quotient by the interval average of e_t. Uniform convergence and finite measure show E differentiable with E'(r)=∫_B e_t.

Differentiate e to get 2u_t·u_tt+2Σu_j·∂_j u_t. Let g_j=u_t·u_j; its derivative equals (∂_j u_t)·u_j+u_t·u_jj and is continuous compactly supported, hence integrable by M001. Coordinate permutation and M003 give Fubini. M002 on an interval containing the support gives ∫∂_j g_j=0. Hence E'(r)=2∫u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu). H001 differentiated gives u·u_t=0; H002 gives acceleration=a u, so integrand vanishes. Therefore E'(r)=0. Since r arbitrary the conclusion follows.
